setting:
The world is cloaked in fog, soot, and silence — a realm of gaslight and deception, where every step echoes with secrets and nothing wears its true face.
The time is a brittle hinge between ages, where horse-drawn carriages give way to steam and steel, and the rules of old no longer hold fast.
The setting is **Victorian London**, a city of crumbling grandeur and restless ambition, where empire casts long shadows and crime blooms beneath the cobblestones.
Society teeters on the edge — class divides blur, science challenges faith, and the line between progress and peril grows thin with every new invention.
Detectives walk this uncertain world like half-mythic figures — thinkers, hunters, liars — cutting through illusion with intuition and blood.
Mystery is everywhere: in the locked room, the vanished heir, the laughing corpse, the trembling maid. Nothing arrives without a cost, and every clue is a coin spent in doubt.
Stories draw from Doyle, Poe, and the ink-stained chronicles of a world trying to explain itself before it falls apart.
Themes spiral through guilt, corruption, obsession, and truth — not just in the crimes solved, but in the ones we choose to ignore.
rules:
Clues:
Every mystery leaves traces in its wake. To peel back the layers of deceit and reach the truth, your character must gather fragments of information — whispered gossip, half-burned notes, overlooked fingerprints — and assemble them into something coherent.

When attempting to uncover a clue, ask a closed question and interpret the result as follows:

- **"No, and..."**: The trail is cold. Nothing surfaces — not even a red herring.
- **"No"**: Something surfaces, but it’s little more than background noise — a detail of no real consequence.
- **"No, but..."**: You find something... but it deceives. A clue that points in the wrong direction.
- **"Yes, but..."**: You find a real clue — but it’s incomplete, distorted, or buried in noise. Further legwork is required.
- **"Yes"**: A clear and useful piece of information emerges. A thread that can be followed.
- **"Yes, and..."**: The investigation leaps forward. A cache of insight, a breakthrough — something that rewrites the board.

Interrogation:
People lie. They withhold. They break under pressure or hide behind smiles. When questioning a suspect or witness, every word must be weighed, every glance watched. Interrogation is a duel — not of blades, but of patience, perception, and precision.

When questioning someone, ask a closed question and consult the result:

- **"No, and..."**: The suspect shuts down completely. The door slams shut.
- **"No"**: They offer scraps — vague, unrelated, useless.
- **"No, but..."**: They lead you astray, deliberately or not. A lie wrapped in truth.
- **"Yes, but..."**: The truth emerges — but slowly, and through resistance. You’ll need to work harder to make sense of it.
- **"Yes"**: They talk. The details make sense. Something valuable comes through.
- **"Yes, and..."**: They spill more than intended — one thread, then another. Suddenly, the whole picture begins to shift.

Alibis:
Everyone has a story. Whether it holds up under scrutiny is another matter. Some will offer details too perfect. Others will be vague in the places that matter most. It's your job to test those stories — to verify alibis, or to unpick the lies woven into them.

When checking an alibi, ask a closed question and interpret the outcome:

- **"No, and..."**: The alibi crumbles before you can confirm a single detail. Nothing adds up.
- **"No"**: The story can’t be verified, but it doesn’t appear to matter — yet.
- **"No, but..."**: You fail to confirm the alibi, but stumble onto something misleading — a false trail.
- **"Yes, but..."**: The alibi checks out... mostly. But something in the way it fits is too neat, or raises other questions.
- **"Yes"**: The alibi holds. It’s solid, plausible, and backed by fact.
- **"Yes, and..."**: The alibi not only checks out, it sheds light on something else — a hidden motive, a second suspect, an unexpected connection.

Evidence:
Blood stains. Scratched floorboards. Fibers clinging to a cuff. The world leaves traces — even when a killer tries to erase them. Your task is to find those traces, read them, and understand what they mean.

When collecting or analyzing physical evidence, ask a closed question and apply the result:

- **"No, and..."**: You find nothing. Worse, you may have disturbed the scene.
- **"No"**: You uncover something — but it’s mundane, or unrelated.
- **"No, but..."**: You uncover something that appears meaningful… but points you the wrong way.
- **"Yes, but..."**: You find something solid, but it’s partial — unclear, damaged, or out of context.
- **"Yes"**: The evidence is clear, usable, and directly advances the case.
- **"Yes, and..."**: Not only is the evidence decisive — it reveals connections, accelerates conclusions, or opens entirely new leads.

locations.label: The Guttering Lamp
locations.detail: A half-abandoned public house at the edge of the fog district, where oil smoke clings to the ceiling and regulars drink without eye contact.
locations.encounters: Rumor-hoarding bartender, washed-up inspector, figure who always sits near the door

locations.label: The Verlaine Theatre
locations.detail: An aging but once-illustrious playhouse known for its velvet drapes, whispered scandals, and a chandelier that once fell mid-performance.
locations.encounters: Forgotten understudy, patron who never applauds, masked stagehand with a locked dressing room

locations.label: The Violet Parlour
locations.detail: A discreet salon for the influential and disreputable alike; officially a tea room, unofficially a place to arrange disappearances or favors.
locations.encounters: Retired spy turned hostess, gossip broker, veiled patron with a coded fan

locations.label: The Brassworks Asylum
locations.detail: A grim, fortified hospital for the mentally unwell — or those made inconvenient. The gates creak even when shut.
locations.encounters: Rambling patient with perfect recall, overworked night doctor, missing records clerk

locations.label: Marwick College of Unnatural Philosophy
locations.detail: A forgotten annex of the city’s university, where outdated disciplines are still practiced and lectures are sometimes interrupted by static.
locations.encounters: Sleep-deprived archivist, lecturer on cursed numbers, assistant with a locked satchel

locations.label: The Argent Hotel
locations.detail: A silver-domed establishment of faded glory, where chandeliers flicker despite rewiring, and guests often check out without packing.
locations.encounters: Concierge who forgets nothing, heiress in mourning, bellboy with too many keys

seeds: Infiltrate a gentlemen’s club to unearth the truth behind a member’s sudden, scandalous death.
Recover a stolen heirloom before it’s auctioned under a false name at a secret collector’s gathering.
Catch a masked burglar whose thefts match a series of unsolved cold cases — down to the minute.
Investigate a girl’s disappearance from a finishing school with locked dorms and a curiously silent staff.
Uncover the source of blackmail targeting a socialite with ties to a forgotten asylum fire.
Trace a rash of arsons to a common link — and stop the next blaze before it consumes Parliament Row.
Retrieve a missing painting rumored to contain the confession of its murdered artist.
Gather evidence against a police officer who has erased more than just reports.
Identify the source of anonymous threats sent to a shipping magnate with wartime secrets.
Hunt a serial killer whose victims all wore the same perfume — discontinued for decades.
Disarm a blackmailer who claims to possess letters that could bring down half the Privy Council.
Find a vanished heiress last seen boarding a train that never arrived.
Expose the ghost thief plundering society balls — whose identity shifts with every witness.
Guard a philanthropist during a masked charity gala — and discover who wants them dead by midnight.
Stop a string of ritualistic murders echoing an occult trial from a century ago.
Trap a con artist seducing and defrauding London’s elite one engagement at a time.
Investigate a missing artifact tied to a deadly curse no museum dares display.
Protect a judge who sentenced a killer now presumed dead — until new killings follow the same pattern.
Retrieve a shipment of falsified medical supplies before they enter a city-wide distribution chain.
Track down stolen research notes before a theoretical invention becomes a practical weapon.
Follow a string of counterfeit inheritances to the printing press that shouldn't exist.
Unmask a thief whose diamond heists follow the arc of an unpublished novel.
Protect a politician receiving threats written in mirror script — and dated a week into the future.
Retrieve a patent prototype stolen from a dead inventor’s lab by someone who shouldn't know it exists.
Catch a gallery curator staging their own thefts to fund a secret collection of forgeries.
Solve the murder of a socialite found dead in a locked suite with a shattered looking glass.
Stop a cat burglar targeting the homes of recently deceased collectors.
Investigate disappearances in the city’s poorest quarter tied to a “ghost tax” collected by strangers in uniform.
Trace the death of a parkland wanderer whose final words match a previous victim’s journal.
Retrieve a stolen painting rumored to shift nightly — and show its thief in real time.
Uncover the truth behind a noble’s death at a secluded estate where no one remembers the night clearly.
Recover a stolen formula before it can be replicated — or silenced — by its competitor.
Investigate disappearances at a university where students claim the library’s basement changes shape.
Break into a noble mansion to retrieve an object someone inside is willing to kill to keep hidden.
Discover who killed a gang lord inside a locked prison cell — and why no one seems surprised.
Identify the woman found in the harbor with no name, no records — and your contact’s address sewn into her hem.

frailties.label: Tormented by a single unsolved case
Has an enemy in the force
Sees patterns where there are none
Too eager to believe in guilt
Feels guilt for a wrongful arrest
Hears footsteps no one else does

gear.label: Ink that only appears in moonlight
Tarnished badge of a defunct precinct

factions.name: The Black Ledger
gear: death certificates filed before the fact
factions.goal: To ensure certain truths never surface — and others become inevitable
factions.motive: Power is perception; history belongs to those who fund it

factions.name: The Silent Service
frailties: Forbidden from exposure — their greatest strength is also a leash
factions.goal: To control what the public believes by controlling what remains discoverable
factions.nemesis: The Ink & Ash Society and any detective who refuses to stand down

factions.name: The Ink & Ash Society
frailties: No central command; easy prey for co-option
factions.goal: To bring buried truth to light — no matter the cost
factions.motive: They believe knowledge *must* be shared, even if it kills them
factions.nemesis: The Black Ledger, who write the truths people believe

factions.name: The Church of Saint Elvan
frailties: Riddled with charlatans and rival interpretations
factions.goal: To prove that truth transcends the material — and can be summoned
factions.motive: Consolation, redemption, and something more cryptic
factions.nemesis: Rationalist societies and former members who saw too much

factions.name: The Ashgrove Club
frailties: Coddled by their privilege; underestimate the desperate
factions.goal: To steer public memory and narrative by controlling secrets at the source
factions.motive: Legacy, inheritance, and the quiet terror of public shame
factions.nemesis: The Ink & Ash Society, and anyone who won’t play by the rules

factions.name: The Rookery Pact
factions.goal: To protect their own and barter truths the world forgot
factions.motive: Some secrets belong to the streets — and no one else
factions.nemesis: The Silent Service, who erase what the Pact remembers

npcs.name: Captain Augustus Blackwood
npcs.motive: He was framed for a cover-up he tried to expose. Now he seeks the truth that cost him everything.
npcs.nemesis: Commissioner Hale, who made the evidence vanish

npcs.name: Miss Prudence Fairfax
npcs.goal: To write the one story no one dares print
npcs.motive: She believes a single name connects three deaths — and she’s willing to destroy reputations to prove it
npcs.nemesis: Lord Wyndham, her former sponsor and current target

npcs.name: Dr. Theodore Marlowe
npcs.goal: To publish irrefutable proof of a serial poisoner among the elite
npcs.motive: A patient he couldn't save left behind a letter... and it haunts him
npcs.nemesis: Dean Ellison of the Royal Medical Society, who calls him "unfit"

npcs.name: Ivy Addams
npcs.goal: To disappear for good — but not before settling one last score
npcs.motive: She knows the man who framed her is about to do it again
npcs.nemesis: Detective Ormsey, who calls her “informant” but means “bait”

npcs.name: Mr. Jeremy Bentley
npcs.concept: Patron of the Arts, Collector of People
npcs.goal: To become indispensable to every circle that matters
npcs.motive: The higher he rises, the further he can bury his family’s crimes
npcs.nemesis: Cousin Gregory, the one person he can’t buy

npcs.name: Miss Margaret Sterling
npcs.goal: To bring systemic rot into daylight — one name at a time
npcs.motive: Her sister died in an asylum that shouldn’t have existed
npcs.nemesis: Sir Alder Brackley, parliamentarian and silent shareholder

monsters.name: The Confidence Man
monsters.goal: To extract wealth, trust, or secrets from the gullible
monsters.nemesis: The one mark who saw through it once before

monsters.name: The Smuggler
frailties: Haunted by a deal gone wrong
monsters.goal: To keep the goods — and themselves — unseen
monsters.motive: Profit... and maybe protection for someone else
monsters.nemesis: A customs agent with a personal score to settle

monsters.name: The Second-Story Artist
frailties: Drawn to notoriety like a moth to flame
monsters.goal: To claim what they believe should never have been guarded
monsters.motive: Money, pride — or inheritance by other means
monsters.nemesis: The retired detective who caught them once... and let them go

monsters.name: The Forger
frailties: Believes no one is truly original
monsters.goal: To seed the world with their handiwork
monsters.motive: The thrill of deception disguised as craft
monsters.nemesis: A curator who knows their style too well

monsters.name: The Blackmailer
monsters.goal: To control through fear, not force
monsters.motive: A need for power that no position could offer
monsters.nemesis: Someone whose past they got wrong — fatally

monsters.name: The Counterfeiter
monsters.goal: To flood the market with falsehoods
monsters.motive: To prove they could always do it better
monsters.nemesis: A banker with a ruined reputation and a long memory
